text:
devon: FYI seeing p99 jump from ~220ms -> ~1.2s on canary runtime v2.9.4 after the 08:15 UTC rollout. Multiple customer pages. Can we triage?

maria: which tenants are affected? any commonality (model size, seq len)?

devon: mostly mid-size seqs (512-1024), multi-tenant pool A, traffic shifted to v2.9.4 at 08:15 by deploy-bot. p95 roughly the same, p99 tail blown out.

infra-bot: deploy-bot: canary rollout v2.9.4 -> 15% traffic @ 08:15 UTC.

jonathan: grabbing traces and flamegraphs from trace store now. devon — can you paste the query you ran for p99?

devon: sure — prometheus: 
```
histogram_quantile(0.99, sum(rate(request_latency_bucket{service="runtime",version="v2.9.4"}[5m])) by (le))
```
I also pulled tail traces: many show long time in "kv_fetch" + "executor_idle" spans.

alyssa: kv_fetch? Did cache miss rate change?

jonathan: looking at kvcache metrics: kvcache.miss_rate for pool A jumped 3x after rollout. prefix-cache hit % dropped.

maria: v2.9.4 changed prefix hashing to reduce hot keys — could that interact with our cache sharding?

devon: yes, the change tweaks key->shard mapping to spread load, but should be transparent. Maybe some skew for certain tenants.

jonathan: I see pods on host gcp-us-west3-07 with much higher io_wait on nvme, correlates with requests to pool A.

alyssa: can we repro locally with synthetic workload? I can run a traffic replay against canary instances.

devon: pls do but be careful, the canary cluster is live. run small RT replay with seq=512 heavy context.

alyssa: running now — initial run shows 10% of requests hitting a slow path where executor waits ~800ms between tokens. attaching snippet: 
```
[2026-03-17T08:22:10Z] request_id=abc123 span=kv_fetch duration=0.82s key=prefix:tenant42:ctx
[2026-03-17T08:22:10Z] request_id=abc123 span=executor_idle duration=0.09s
```

jonathan: interesting — the slow kv_fetch is hitting a remote store fallback (we fallback to S3-backed cold store on misses). Why would misses spike?

devon: pool A had recently had a config change to increase max_sequences_per_shard, could push older prefixes off memory. Combined with new hashing could relocate many prefixes -> cold misses.

maria: check retention/eviction logs on kvcache: /var/log/kvcache/evict.log on the affected pods.

jonathan: grep shows mass evictions exactly at 08:14:58 UTC on several pods, followed by repopulation. Eviction reason=shard_rebalance.

sre-oncall: assigning incident INC-2026-245 to triage. Immediate mitigation options: 1) rollback v2.9.4 canary traffic 2) increase kvcache size on pool A 3) throttle rebalance. Thoughts?

devon: immediate rollback to previous hashing behavior seems safest. Can we do a targeted rollback for pool A?

infra-bot: deploy-bot: initiating config rollback for runtime.v2.9.4 -> routing revert for pool A at 08:31 UTC (15% -> 0% on v2.9.4).

maria: i'm worried about slow warm-up after rollback if cache already evicted. If we rollback, misses may continue until clients repopulate. We should also bump kvcache capacity temporarily and disable rebalance.

alyssa: I can create a canary patch to disable shard_rebalance in kvcache config and push to pool A hosts. That should stop further churn.

jonathan: while you do that, i'm adding a metric alert: if eviction_rate > 50/s for 2m, page SRE. Also capturing a sample set of affected request_ids for deeper analysis.

devon: customer comms: I'm drafting a note to affected accounts saying we're investigating and applying mitigations.

infra-bot: deploy-bot: patch kvcache.disable_rebalance=true applied to pool A hosts at 08:34 UTC.

alyssa: patch deployed. eviction rate dropped to baseline after ~90s. p99 back down to ~260ms within 4 minutes.

maria: excellent. jonathan — do you still see any pods with high io_wait?

jonathan: a couple of hosts still show elevated io_wait but trending down. No more S3 fallbacks in traces after 08:38.

devon: resolution so far: rollback routing of v2.9.4 for pool A + disable rebalance. p99 restored. Root cause appears to be interaction of new prefix hashing + aggressive shard_rebalance config leading to mass evictions and cold cache misses.

maria: action items: 
- ENGINEERING-4287: revert hashing change in v2.9.4 and rework rollout strategy (owner: devon)
- ENGINEERING-4288: make kvcache rebalance throttled and safe-guard with gradual cutover (owner: alyssa)
- SRE-2026: add eviction_rate alert + playbook (owner: jonathan)
- CS-comm: send follow-up to affected customers with timeline and mitigation (owner: devon)

jonathan: filing incident report and attaching traces + evict logs.

devon: thanks team. I'll keep the thread updated once the revert PR lands and we have a safer rollout plan. :thumbsup:
